title: PyTorch Tutorials
description: Official tutorial hub covering tensors, autograd, building and training neural networks, datasets and dataloaders, saving models and deployment.
why_useful: The shortest route from understanding gradients on paper to actually training something, using the framework most research code and job postings assume.
learning_outcomes: Build and train a network with autograd
Write a dataset and dataloader for your own data
Save, load and run a trained model

title: Transfer Learning for Computer Vision Tutorial
description: Official PyTorch tutorial demonstrating fine-tuning a pretrained convolutional network and using one as a fixed feature extractor, with the training loop shown in full.
why_useful: Makes the two distinct strategies concrete side by side — freezing a backbone versus fine-tuning it — which is the decision that most affects results when data is limited.
learning_outcomes: Fine-tune a pretrained model on a small dataset
Use a pretrained network as a frozen feature extractor
Judge which of the two a given data budget calls for

title: Dive into Deep Learning
description: Interactive open book combining explanation, mathematics and runnable code, covering linear networks, convolutional and recurrent architectures, attention, transformers and optimisation.
author: Aston Zhang, Zachary C. Lipton, Mu Li, Alexander J. Smola
quality_notes: Large. Best used as a course you work through selectively rather than a book read cover to cover.
why_useful: One of the few resources where the mathematics and a working implementation sit on the same page, so you can check your understanding against code immediately instead of much later.
learning_outcomes: Connect the mathematics of a layer to its code

title: Neural Networks: Zero To Hero
description: Video course building neural networks from first principles in code, starting from a scalar autograd engine and progressing to language models and transformers.
author: Andrej Karpathy
quality_notes: Long-form and code-along. It rewards typing along rather than watching passively.
why_useful: Builds backpropagation and then a transformer from nothing, in code, so the machinery stops being a black box. Few resources remove this much mystery per hour spent.
learning_outcomes: Build a small language model end to end
Explain what each part of a transformer block does

title: Stanford CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
description: University course covering image classification, loss functions, optimisation, backpropagation, convolutional networks, training practice and modern vision architectures.
quality_notes: Materials available publicly vary by year; assignments and lecture videos are not always posted for the current offering.
why_useful: Its notes on training practice — initialisation, normalisation, regularisation and debugging — remain among the clearest available, and transfer well beyond vision.
learning_outcomes: Diagnose a training run that is not converging

title: The Illustrated Transformer
description: Visual walkthrough of the transformer architecture, stepping through self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding, and the encoder-decoder stack.
author: Jay Alammar
quality_notes: Community-created explainer, not an official or peer-reviewed source. Excellent as an on-ramp; read the original paper for precision.
why_useful: The most effective bridge between not understanding attention and being able to read the original paper. Its diagrams are the ones most people end up picturing afterwards.
learning_outcomes: Explain query, key and value in your own words
Trace a token's path through an encoder block
